gaps: Creating a circle also adds a membership, but the spec only says joining is refused at the 20-circle limit. It does not say what happens when a member with 20 circles creates one, or require that case in acceptance criteria (docs/specs/circles.md:23, docs/specs/circles.md:27, docs/specs/circles.md:118).

The security requirement that an invite code 'cannot practically be guessed' has no measurable strength or abuse limit. An implementer cannot tell what code length, randomness, or guessing protection passes this requirement (docs/specs/circles.md:31).

The 'invite' event is defined for copying or sharing, but the spec does not say whether a cancelled WhatsApp share, a failed copy, or repeated taps count. Those choices change the per-circle invite counter used to judge MVP spread (docs/specs/circles.md:37, docs/decisions/0008-first-party-usage-counters.md:17).

The invalid-link response covers reset links and deleted circles but leaves unknown or malformed codes unspecified. A distinct response could reveal whether a circle or former link exists (docs/specs/circles.md:52).

The spec does not explicitly require the direct join operation to validate the current invite code, completed account, removal block, and both capacity limits at the moment membership is added. Concurrent joins could exceed 100 members or 20 circles even if the preview and button enforce those checks (docs/specs/circles.md:46, docs/specs/circles.md:55, docs/specs/circles.md:57).

It is unclear whether 'allow them back' restores a removed person's membership immediately or merely clears the block so they must use an invite and press Join. The choice affects consent to rejoin, capacity checks, card visibility, and whether a new join event is recorded (docs/specs/circles.md:57, docs/specs/circles.md:77).

The spec says members see the member list but does not explicitly deny non-members that list through direct data requests. The preview criterion checks only what the screen shows, leaving a route to members' display names unless the data boundary is stated (docs/specs/circles.md:43, docs/specs/circles.md:62, docs/specs/circles.md:104).

The spec does not say whether a person who voluntarily leaves can use a still-valid invite to rejoin, or whether leaving creates the same block as removal. That changes the leave flow and the admin's removed-people list (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:74).

Renaming has no stated trim, length, or empty-name rule, although creation requires a 1 to 40 character name. A direct rename could leave a circle with a name creation would reject (docs/specs/circles.md:23, docs/specs/circles.md:78).

Deleting a circle ends memberships, but the spec does not say whether its historical per-circle usage counts remain visible to the owner and, if so, under what circle label. Deleting the circle record could make the required per-circle metrics unintelligible or erase them (docs/specs/circles.md:80, docs/decisions/0008-first-party-usage-counters.md:17).

Automatic succession uses the member who 'joined earliest' without a tie rule or a stated result for concurrent leave, deletion, or handover. Those operations must still preserve exactly one admin (docs/specs/circles.md:25, docs/specs/circles.md:79, docs/specs/circles.md:85).

A removal block needs to survive link resets, but the spec does not say what happens to it when that person deletes their account and later signs up again. Retaining an identity link may conflict with account erasure; discarding it lets the same person bypass the block (docs/specs/circles.md:57, docs/specs/accounts.md:117, docs/specs/accounts.md:126).

The acceptance criteria do not cover the specified confirmation steps for leaving, removing a member, and deleting a circle, nor the circle's deletion and link invalidation when its sole member deletes their account. Those user flows could be omitted while the listed criteria still pass (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:74, docs/specs/circles.md:80, docs/specs/circles.md:122, docs/specs/accounts.md:110).
contradictions: The draft says only the admin can see, copy, or share the invite link, including in criterion 2, yet invitees must receive and open that same URL and can copy or forward it outside the app. The restriction needs a scope such as retrieving the active link and using in-app controls (docs/specs/circles.md:33, docs/specs/circles.md:43, docs/specs/circles.md:101).

The invite preview exposes the admin's display name to a person who has not joined, while the confirmed Accounts contract permits a member's display name to be returned only to people who currently share a circle with them. A removed person with a valid link also regains circle metadata despite the stated immediate loss of access (docs/specs/circles.md:43, docs/specs/circles.md:74, docs/specs/accounts.md:93).

An existing member is sent straight to the circle when opening an invite link, while a reset link must always show the no-longer-valid message and reveal nothing. The draft gives no precedence when an existing member opens an old link (docs/specs/circles.md:51, docs/specs/circles.md:52, docs/specs/circles.md:110).

The admin can see a list of removed people and allow them back, but removed people no longer share that circle. Showing their display names conflicts with the confirmed rule that names are returned only to members who currently share a circle; retaining those names after account deletion also conflicts with erasure (docs/specs/circles.md:77, docs/specs/accounts.md:93, docs/specs/accounts.md:117).

Criterion 6 says a departing or removed member and the circle's members stop seeing each other's data without qualifying that they may share another circle. The behavior text limits the loss to visibility 'through that circle', and the confirmed Accounts and Cards specs require visibility to continue while any shared circle remains (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:113, docs/specs/accounts.md:93, docs/specs/cards.md:82).

Join re-checks link, completed account, removal block and both limits at the moment of joining; simultaneous joins never exceed limits.
Clear all removals only lifts blocks; unblocked people rejoin via a valid link and Join, with normal checks and a join event.
Non-members never receive the member list or member names, including via direct data requests.
Voluntary leaving creates no block; the person can rejoin through a valid link.
Rename follows the 1 to 40 character rule.
Deleted circles keep past usage events, shown under the last name marked '(deleted)'.
Succession uses earliest join time with a consistent tie pick; leave, removal, handover and deletion apply one at a time so exactly one admin remains.
A removal block is erased with account deletion per the confirmed Accounts erasure rule; a re-signup is a new person; the admin can reset the link.
Added criteria for confirmation steps and sole-member account deletion deleting the circle.
Scoped the restriction to in-app retrieval of the active link; forwarding outside the app is expected and reset is the remedy.
Removed the admin's name from the join preview; removed people see only "You can't join this circle."
Link validity is checked first for everyone, members included, so an old link always shows the invalid message.
No removed-people list or names; blocks are lifted all at once by the admin, and erased on account deletion.
AC6 and Leave now limit loss of visibility to that circle; visibility through other shared circles continues.

It is unclear whether 'allow them back' restores a removed person's membership immediately or merely clears the block so they must use an invite and press Join. The choice affects consent to rejoin, capacity checks, card visibility, and whether a new join event is recorded (docs/specs/circles.md:57, docs/specs/circles.md:77).

The spec does not say whether a person who voluntarily leaves can use a still-valid invite to rejoin, or whether leaving creates the same block as removal. That changes the leave flow and the admin's removed-people list (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:74).

Renaming has no stated trim, length, or empty-name rule, although creation requires a 1 to 40 character name. A direct rename could leave a circle with a name creation would reject (docs/specs/circles.md:23, docs/specs/circles.md:78).

Automatic succession uses the member who 'joined earliest' without a tie rule or a stated result for concurrent leave, deletion, or handover. Those operations must still preserve exactly one admin (docs/specs/circles.md:25, docs/specs/circles.md:79, docs/specs/circles.md:85).

The acceptance criteria do not cover the specified confirmation steps for leaving, removing a member, and deleting a circle, nor the circle's deletion and link invalidation when its sole member deletes their account. Those user flows could be omitted while the listed criteria still pass (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:74, docs/specs/circles.md:80, docs/specs/circles.md:122, docs/specs/accounts.md:110).

An existing member is sent straight to the circle when opening an invite link, while a reset link must always show the no-longer-valid message and reveal nothing. The draft gives no precedence when an existing member opens an old link (docs/specs/circles.md:51, docs/specs/circles.md:52, docs/specs/circles.md:110).

Criterion 6 says a departing or removed member and the circle's members stop seeing each other's data without qualifying that they may share another circle. The behavior text limits the loss to visibility 'through that circle', and the confirmed Accounts and Cards specs require visibility to continue while any shared circle remains (docs/specs/circles.md:68, docs/specs/circles.md:113, docs/specs/accounts.md:93, docs/specs/cards.md:82).

The preview criterion checks only what the screen shows, leaving a route to members' display names unless the data boundary is stated (docs/specs/circles.md:43, docs/specs/circles.md:62, docs/specs/circles.md:104).

A removal block needs to survive link resets, but the spec does not say what happens to it when that person deletes their account and later signs up again.      nothing else about it.
  5. Anyone else sees the circle name and the number of members, but no
     member names, and can press "Join".

  whatever the screen showed: the link is still the active one, the person has
  a completed account, they are not blocked by a removal, the circle has fewer
  than 100 members and they belong to fewer than 20 circles. Simultaneous joins
  can never push a circle past 100 members or a person past 20 circles.
- A refused join shows a clear message naming the reason (circle full, or too
  many circles).
